title: Note On Fair Copy And Correspondence

questions.question: Why does the note say some topics from other books of the Risale-i Nur appear again in this treatise?
questions.answer: Because the other parts were not available where this treatise was being written, so some important points had to be included here too.

questions.question: How does the note explain that the repeated material is still useful?
questions.answer: It says the students in that area would be able to write a small but complete version of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: Who wrote the revised copy of the rough draft?
questions.answer: A blessed person wrote it.

questions.question: What is surprising about the person who prepared the revised copy?
questions.answer: He did not know much about these matters, yet something meaningful still appeared in his writing.

questions.question: What special pattern was noticed in the revised copy?
questions.answer: The number of alifs at the beginnings of the lines came to six hundred and sixty-six.

questions.question: What is an alif, according to the footnote?
questions.answer: It is the first letter of the Arabic alphabet, written as a straight vertical mark, and it also has the number value of one.

questions.question: Why is the number 666 important in the note?
questions.answer: It matches the abjad value of the title Ayat al-Kubra.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from this number matching the title?
questions.answer: It is taken as a sign that the title fits the treatise well.

questions.question: Besides matching the title, what other meaning is understood from the same number?
questions.answer: It is seen as a sign that the treatise is a light or reflection coming from the Qur’anic verses.

questions.question: What larger number in the note is connected to the Qur’an, and how?
questions.answer: The number 6,666 is connected to the verses of the Qur’an.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the whole note?
questions.answer: The note explains why some repetition happened and points to a meaningful numerical sign connected to the treatise’s title and the Qur’an.

questions.question: What problem in that location made it necessary to include some material again in this treatise?
questions.answer: The other sections of the Risale-i Nur were not there.

questions.question: Which works are named as containing some of the important matters mentioned again here?
questions.answer: The Words and The Flashes.

questions.question: Why were students in that region asked to write down the whole treatise anyway?
questions.answer: So they could produce a compact but complete copy of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What detail about the beginnings of the lines was counted?
questions.answer: The alifs at the start of the lines were counted.

questions.question: What does the note suggest by calling the person who wrote the revised copy “blessed”?
questions.answer: It suggests that his work was seen as favored and meaningful, not ordinary.

questions.question: Why does the note mention that he was not knowledgeable in these topics?
questions.answer: To show that the pattern was not likely planned by him on purpose.

questions.question: What system is used to connect the title with a number?
questions.answer: The abjad system is used.

questions.question: Which title is said to have the same number value as the counted alifs?
questions.answer: Ayat al-Kubra, or The Supreme Sign.

questions.question: What belief about the treatise comes from this numerical harmony?
questions.answer: That the title suits it and that the treatise has a special connection to Qur’anic light.

questions.question: According to the note, was the repetition in the treatise presented as careless writing or as something done for a reason?
questions.answer: It was presented as something done for a reason.

questions.question: What was that reason?
questions.answer: Important subjects had to be included because the other related books were unavailable there.

questions.question: What educational benefit did the writer want for the local students?
questions.answer: He wanted them to write out a miniature complete Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What stage of writing came before the revised copy?
questions.answer: A rough draft came first.

questions.question: What kind of person prepared the revised version?
questions.answer: A blessed person prepared it.

questions.question: What makes the letter pattern in the revised copy seem remarkable?
questions.answer: It appeared even though the copyist was not trained in such special matters.

questions.question: Where exactly were the counted alifs found?
questions.answer: At the beginning of the lines.

questions.question: How many of these alifs were counted?
questions.answer: Six hundred and sixty-six.

questions.question: What two things are linked by this number in the note?
questions.answer: The title Ayat al-Kubra and the number of verses of the Qur’an.

questions.question: What is meant here by saying the title corresponds by abjad value?
questions.answer: It means the letters of the title add up numerically to the same total.

questions.question: What does the writer understand this correspondence to indicate about the treatise?
questions.answer: That it is a reflection or ray coming from the light of the Qur’an.

questions.question: What is one strong theme running through the whole note?
questions.answer: The treatise is shown as both carefully preserved and spiritually meaningful.

questions.question: Why does the note begin by talking about other parts of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: To explain why this treatise includes some ideas that had already appeared elsewhere.

questions.question: What made those other parts unusable in that situation?
questions.answer: They were not present in the place where this treatise was composed.

questions.question: What does the phrase about writing a “complete” small Risale-i Nur suggest about this treatise?
questions.answer: It suggests the treatise was meant to help gather essential teachings in one accessible form.

questions.question: After the explanation about repetition, what new subject does the note move to?
questions.answer: It moves to the revised copy and a meaningful number pattern in it.

questions.question: What was noticed in the revised copy that gave it special importance?
questions.answer: A precise count of alifs appeared at the starts of the lines.

questions.question: Why would counting letters matter in this note?
questions.answer: Because the number is used as a sign connected to the title and to Qur’anic meaning.

questions.question: What title is said to have been given by Imam Ali?
questions.answer: Ayat al-Kubra, meaning The Supreme Sign.

questions.question: What does the note say this title’s number value does?
questions.answer: It matches the number of alifs in the copy.

questions.question: How does the writer use that match as evidence?
questions.answer: He treats it as proof that the title is fitting for the treatise.

questions.question: What second layer of meaning is found in the same number pattern?
questions.answer: It also points to the treatise being linked to the light of the Qur’an’s verses.

questions.question: Why is the number 6,666 brought in at the end of the note?
questions.answer: To connect the smaller number pattern with the total number of Qur’anic verses mentioned there.

questions.question: What overall message does the note give about the treatise?
questions.answer: It presents the treatise as necessary, purposeful, and connected in a special way to the Qur’an.

questions.question: What caused some important teachings to be restated in The Supreme Sign?
questions.answer: The needed volumes of the Risale-i Nur were not available where this work was being written.

questions.question: Which two named works are said to have important points repeated here?
questions.answer: The Words and The Flashes.

questions.question: What was the purpose of having students write down the whole treatise?
questions.answer: The purpose was to let them produce a shortened but complete collection of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: Who produced the revised version of the draft?
questions.answer: A blessed person did.

questions.question: What detail makes the writer think the pattern in the copy was not just planned by human skill?
questions.answer: The copyist was not knowledgeable in these special subjects.

questions.question: What exact letter was counted in the copy?
questions.answer: The letter alif was counted.

questions.question: How many alifs were found at the beginnings of the lines?
questions.answer: There were 666.

questions.question: What does the note say this number fully agrees with?
questions.answer: It fully agrees with the abjad value of the treatise’s title.

questions.question: What judgment does the writer make because of that agreement?
questions.answer: He says it shows the title suits the treatise.

questions.question: What spiritual meaning is then added to this numerical agreement?
questions.answer: It is taken as a sign that the treatise comes as a gleam from the Qur’an.

questions.question: How do both parts of the note fit together—the repetition and the number pattern?
questions.answer: The first part explains the practical need for the treatise, and the second part points to a meaningful sign supporting its importance.

questions.question: In the note, what practical challenge led to apparent repetition?
questions.answer: The challenge was that other parts of the Risale-i Nur were missing in that place.

questions.question: Why does the note call the repetition only “apparent”?
questions.answer: Because it was not useless repeating; it served a clear purpose.

questions.question: What was that clear purpose for the students in the area?
questions.answer: They were to write out a miniature full Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What happened after the rough draft stage?
questions.answer: A revised copy was made.

questions.question: How is the person who made that revised copy described in both spiritual and educational terms?
questions.answer: He is described as blessed, but not trained in those technical matters.

questions.question: What hidden order was found in his copy?
questions.answer: The line openings contained 666 alifs.

questions.question: Why is that hidden order treated as meaningful instead of random?
questions.answer: Because it matches the numerical value of the title through the abjad system.

questions.question: Which title is being confirmed by that match?
questions.answer: Ayat al-Kubra, or The Supreme Sign.

questions.question: What does the note say this match demonstrates?
questions.answer: It demonstrates that the title is well suited to the treatise.

questions.question: What further understanding does the writer take from this number?
questions.answer: He understands it as a sign that the treatise is connected to the Qur’an’s light.

questions.question: If a student asked for the central lesson of the note, what would be a good answer?
questions.answer: The note teaches that the treatise was preserved for a real need and that its writing showed signs the author saw as meaningful and Qur’an-related.
